source.title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
source.summary: Modern LLM coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenHands share a common inefficiency: they spend much of their token budget finding the file to patch, rather than patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified, a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, with many calls spent on grep, glob, and view_file during repository exploration. We introduce CodeGrep, a 14B retrieval agent trained end-to-end with GRPO to issue multi-turn parallel grep, glob, and read tool calls and return candidate files to a frozen downstream coding agent. On all 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances, CodeGrep preserves resolve rate while substantially improving efficiency: 27.0% versus 25.8% for the no-retrieval baseline, with 15% fewer rounds and 19% fewer tokens on resolved instances. Across retrievers, downstream utility follows a precision threshold: BM25 with precision 0.375 degrades the agent, Jina with precision 0.445 is neutral, and CodeGrep with precision 0.677 crosses the threshold at which retrieval begins to reduce rollout cost. To enable this study, we mine supervision from 67K open-source agent trajectories using CATM and build a Git-worktree environment for multi-turn agent RL. In our setting, applying the efficiency signal at the advantage layer rather than the reward layer reduces KL drift and translates cleanly into downstream efficiency. We will release the model, training pipeline, RL environment, and evaluation harnesses.

previous_facts.title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
previous_facts.event_hint: A 14B RL-trained agent-style code retriever (CodeGrep) that emits multi-turn parallel grep/glob/read calls and feeds candidate files to a frozen OpenHands agent, cutting rounds and tokens on SWE-Bench Verified while slightly lifting resolve rate.
previous_facts.problem: LLM coding agents (Claude Code, OpenHands) spend most of their token budget finding the file to patch rather than patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, dominated by grep/glob/view_file calls in ambiguous exploration loops, often 20+ rounds in a wrong direction before giving up. No open, systematically-studied agent-style code retriever exists at scale to shorten this phase.
previous_facts.mechanism: CodeGrep is a 14B-parameter retriever built on Qwen3-14B-Instruct, trained end-to-end with GRPO in a custom Git-worktree RL environment. It exposes three read-only primitives (grep regex search, glob path matching, read file contents), emitting up to 8 concurrent tool calls per turn and up to 4 turns (3 exploration + 1 answer). Candidate files are injected into the prompt of a frozen, untouched OpenHands downstream agent, so any downstream effect is unambiguously attributable to the retriever. Supervision is mined via CATM from 67K open-source OpenHands trajectories (one-to-many attribution). A reward-design study (v1->v2->v3) shows that applying the efficiency signal at the advantage layer rather than the reward layer holds KL drift to roughly one-third, and that dropping an auxiliary line-range component improves both stability and downstream efficiency.

evidence.claim: On all 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances, CodeGrep v3 lifts resolve rate by +1.2pp (25.8%->27.0%) while cutting resolved rounds 23.0->19.6 (-15%) and resolved tokens 631K->514K (-19%) versus the no-retrieval OpenHands baseline.
evidence.baseline: No-retrieval OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507: 25.8% resolve, 23.0 rounds, 631K tokens per resolved instance
evidence.condition: 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances; resolved-instances accounting; frozen downstream agent
evidence.source_locator: Section 4.3 / Table 3, PDF Page 6 (also stated in Abstract and Contributions, PDF Page 1-2)

evidence.claim: Downstream utility follows a precision threshold across three retrievers: BM25 (file-precision 0.375) degrades the agent (resolve -0.6pp, resolved tokens +21%, 631K->763K); Jina (0.445) is neutral (resolve identical to baseline 25.8%, tokens -7%); only CodeGrep (0.677) crosses the threshold at which retrieval buys efficiency.
evidence.value: BM25 0.375 hurts; Jina 0.445 neutral; CodeGrep 0.677 helps
evidence.condition: Injected into the same frozen OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B agent
evidence.source_locator: Section 5.1 and Section 4.3, PDF Page 6; precision figures from Table 2

evidence.claim: Intrinsic retrieval quality (Table 2): CodeGrep v3 reaches file-precision 0.677, recall 0.435, F-beta mean 0.576, 43.0% of cases at F-beta>=0.8, in 2.3 agentic turns, versus BM25 (precision 0.375, recall 0.386, 7.0% F-beta>=0.8) and Jina-1.5B (precision 0.445, recall 0.468, 7.0%).
evidence.value: CodeGrep v3 precision 0.677 / recall 0.435 / 43.0% F-beta>=0.8 / 2.3 turns
evidence.condition: Internal evaluation set; turns column applies only to the agentic retriever

evidence.claim: Reward-design study: reward-layer multiplicative scaling of a tool-call penalty (v1) drives KL-to-reference to ~0.31 by step 900, while advantage-layer scaling (v2/v3) holds KL at 0.09/0.15 (~one-third); v3 also converges higher on reward (0.60-0.65 vs 0.45-0.48 for v1/v2) and stabilizes tool-use turns at ~2.1 vs rebound to ~2.6 for v1/v2.
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.5 and Figure 2, PDF Pages 2 and 5; Table 1, PDF Page 5

evidence.claim: Engineering scale: supervision mined from 67,074 raw OpenHands trajectories, filtered by a GLM-5.1-FP8 judge (16-way parallel, thresholds reasoning_tokens>=30 and w>=0.15) to 31,977 effective training samples (47.7% retention); training runs on a single 8xB200 node for ~27 hours wall-clock, early-stopped at step 897 of a planned 2000-step budget.
evidence.value: 31,977 effective samples (47.7% retention); 27h on 8xB200; stop at step 897/2000
evidence.condition: LoRA + optimizer offload + vLLM-colocated rollout on ms-swift; CATM pipeline
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.6 PDF Page 5; Table 5 PDF Page 12

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Benchmark: SWE-Bench Verified (all 500 instances). Downstream agent: OpenHands with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, temperature 0, 100-round max; no-retrieval baseline 25.8% resolve / 23.0 rounds / 631K tokens per resolved issue (within one SD of publicly reported 25.2+-0.7%). Retriever: CodeGrep 14B built on Qwen3-14B-Instruct. Six configurations compared (baseline, BM25, Jina-1.5B, CodeGrep v1/v2/v3). Training hardware: single 8xB200 node, LoRA, ~27h. RL environment uses Git worktrees with up to 8 concurrent tool calls/turn, max 4 turns, tool-concurrency cap 64 (asyncio semaphore), max 32 tool execs per rollout.
previous_facts.limitations: Only one downstream agent stack is evaluated (OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B), so generalization to Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf is untested. The benefit of dropping the line-range reward term is conjectured to be editor-interface dependent: agents whose editor consumes full files (OpenHands, Cursor) benefit, while agents whose editor consumes line ranges (plausibly Windsurf Cascade) may not. v1 matches v3's resolve rate (27.0%) but not its efficiency (-1.3% rounds, -0.6% tokens, essentially flat), showing resolve rate alone does not predict efficiency. Comparison to concurrent Cognition SWE-grep is necessarily partial because their reward formulation is not fully disclosed. Inference-time wall-clock latency is not reported; efficiency is measured only via rounds and tokens.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly targets the agent-acceleration problem of repeated grep/glob/read exploration: it gives an open, trainable retriever that shortens the file-finding phase and reports the exact metrics the topic values (rounds, tokens, tool-call counts, resolve rate). The precision-threshold characterization (hurts/neutral/buys efficiency) is a portable design heuristic for deciding when retrieval injection into a coding agent will pay off. The advantage-layer (vs reward-layer) efficiency-scaling result is a transferable RL-training insight for any tool-policy reward mixing accuracy with efficiency. For a code-agent optimization path (search symbol -> read file -> locate call chain -> patch -> verify), this validates front-loading retrieval into a specialized submodule.
source_notes: Primary source: arXiv 2608.05886v1 (fetched, FETCHED). Evidence Pack covers PDF Pages 1, 2, 5, 6, 10, 12 (abstract, intro, related work, method 3.1-3.6, experiments 4.1-4.3, analysis 5.1, appendix Table 5).
Resolve-rate and efficiency headline numbers in the abstract are corroborated by Table 3 / Section 4.3 with full baselines, so they are treated as verified experiment facts, not unverified claims.
Authors plan to release model, CATM pipeline, RL environment, and evaluation harnesses.
